steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Permanent joints cannot be disassembled without damage: welding, brazing, soft soldering, riveting and adhesive bonding. | Key Fact: Temporary joints can be repeatedly assembled and disassembled: bolts, nuts, screws, clips and captive fasteners. | Key Fact: Welding fuses metals together by melting the parent material (and usually a filler rod); MIG, TIG and MMA are common arc welding processes. | Key Fact: Brazing joins metals by melting a filler (brass alloy, above 450 degrees C) that flows by capillary action between closely fitting parts.
